Stryy Old Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · L'vivs'ka oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Established in the early 18th century, this is the older of Stryy's two Jewish cemeteries — the same community that, by 1921, had grown to nearly 11,000, about 30 percent of the town's population. Nazi occupation from July 1941 brought an early massacre by local residents, a ghetto that by June 1942 held nearly 9,700 Jews, and its liquidation in mid-1943, when roughly 3,000 were killed; only a few dozen Jews are recorded as having survived the war. The cemetery itself was demolished, likely during the war, and later built over with residential flats under Soviet administration.
